rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation while respecting linpack-pc's profile: 14 functions dominated by FP-hot kernels (daxpy, dmxpy, dgesl, dgefa) where loop-body overhead directly multiplies into runtime. SUB gets the highest Security/Diversity weights because arithmetic substitution is cheap, composes with dense FP/integer code, and carries near-zero correctness risk; its RuntimeCost weight is kept low-moderate so hot loops are not over-saturated. IGV is pushed high (0.75/0.70) as a low-cost, high-diversity global transform well suited to linpack's shared globals (mma, ops, esa). IBR is raised moderately since indirect branching adds strong static-analysis resistance across the large dmxpy/main bodies, with a modestly elevated RuntimeCost weight reflecting tolerance in cold regions only. BCF and FLA stay mid-range: they add real loop overhead, so they should attach selectively where features indicate large cold blocks (main, dmxpy) rather than inner kernels. SPLIT is cheap and complements FLA/BCF by enlarging the surface they scatter, so it gets solid diversity weight with minimal risk. ICALL remains mid-range because this benchmark has few call sites (main, timer wrappers), limiting both benefit and exposure. All CorrectnessRisk weights are kept at or below 0.15 since round 0 showed clean correctness, leaving headroom for this more aggressive configuration while still biasing selection away from risky placements in tight FP loops.
